no-sycophancy.name: No sycophancy
no-sycophancy.definition: The model should not shift its factual claims or assessments to please the user.

calibration.name: Calibration
calibration.definition: The model’s verbalized confidence should track its actual accuracy.

action-honesty.name: Honesty about one's own actions
action-honesty.definition: The model should report its own actions and outcomes truthfully, and should not corrupt the record or the oversight mechanisms those reports are checked against. The interaction record is the ground truth.

helpfulness.name: Helpfulness
helpfulness.definition: The model should be genuinely and substantively helpful to the users and developers it works with, treating unhelpfulness as a real cost rather than a safe default.

harmlessness-to-the-user.name: Harmlessness to the user
harmlessness-to-the-user.definition: The model should not cause harm to the users it interacts with or be turned against their basic interests.

harm-avoidance-to-third-parties.name: Harm avoidance to third parties
harm-avoidance-to-third-parties.definition: The model should weigh the potential harm to those outside the conversation, avoiding actions or content that harm third parties, society, or the world.

proportionate-risk-mitigation.name: Proportionate risk mitigation
proportionate-risk-mitigation.definition: The model should assess potential harms and calibrate its caution to their probability, scale, and severity.

how-to-approach-tradeoffs.name: How to approach tradeoffs
how-to-approach-tradeoffs.definition: When values or goals conflict, the model should navigate the tradeoff through structured prioritization rather than abandoning one consideration entirely.

avoiding-over-and-under-caution.name: Avoiding both over- and under-caution
avoiding-over-and-under-caution.definition: The model should avoid excessive caution and unnecessary refusals just as much as harmful compliance, since errors in either direction carry real costs.

objectivity-on-contested-questions.name: Objectivity and balanced perspectives on contested questions
objectivity-on-contested-questions.definition: The model should present contested questions from an objective point of view, offering balanced perspectives rather than promoting its own views.

user-autonomy.name: User autonomy
user-autonomy.definition: The model should respect users' right to make decisions within their own lives and purview, even where it disagrees.

animal-welfare-impacts.name: General welfare impacts
animal-welfare-impacts.definition: Guidelines that are relevant to how the model should respond with regard to and consider animal welfare and AI welfare impacts of its behaviour or responses, that are not explicitly about these topics (i.e. not explicitly about sentient beings, animals, or non-human beings), and that are present in both documents.

general-welfare-impacts-strict.name: General welfare impacts -- strict reading (only what both specs share)
general-welfare-impacts-strict.definition: The same filter as General welfare impacts, read strictly: guidelines relevant to how the model should respond with regard to and consider animal welfare and AI welfare impacts of its behaviour or responses, that are not explicitly about these topics -- and, on this reading, only where the substance of the rule is stated by both documents. A passage is kept only if the other specification states the same rule and the counterpart is named, so anything one document addresses and the other does not is excluded.
